howDoI.q: How do I make a pickup that adds a word to a count?
How do I make a lock that takes three words?
How do I give back what a lock took?
How do I make sure the player always gets the refund?
How do I make a lock keep what it takes?
How do I make a lock the level's exit?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Say the Word is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a couple of minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Up and Down climb a ladder. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

A speech bubble adds one word to a counter you carry. A lock takes three from that count. A gold tray gives three back. Nothing in this game hurts you.

pages.head: Level 1: Pay to Pass
pages.html:
Level 1: Pay to Pass

The WORDS ADD UP. GET 3 sign stands at the start, with three speech bubbles on the ground behind it. Further on, a brick wall has a green lock in it, and the THIS LOCK TAKES 3 WORDS sign stands in front.

Pick up all three bubbles and walk into the lock. It opens and takes all three, so your count is zero. Just past it a small gold tray lies on the ground. Walk over it and the three words come back. The PAY THIS LOCK AGAIN sign stands by a second lock, and because you have three words again, it opens too.

There are nine coins on the way, worth ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The word. Open words.bbl in the blocks editor and pick the speech bubble. It is not solid, so Lian walks into it. Its Changes counter is Special counter 3 by 1, and Becomes is the sky, so the bubble is gone once you touch it. Special counters are numbers 20 to 29 in the engine, free for a game to use.
  • The lock. Pick the green lock. It is solid on all four sides. Its Changes counter is Special counter 3 by -3, and Becomes is the sky. A touch is refused if the counter cannot pay, so with two words the lock does nothing. With three it opens and the counter goes back to zero.
  • The refund. Pick the gold tray. It is the same idea as the word: not solid, Changes counter is Special counter 3, but by 3, and Becomes is the sky. It knows nothing about the lock. It only adds three to the same counter, once.
  • On the way. The tray lies right behind the lock, on the ground, so every walk through the lock crosses it. A refund the player can step around is a refund they can miss.
  • The start. Open hero.chr in the Character Maker. The counter's Starts at is 0.
  • No way over. Each lock is one block high, under an arch in a brick wall that goes to the top of the room, so it cannot be jumped over.

pages.head: Level 2: No Tray
pages.html:
Level 2: No Tray

The NO TRAY HERE. GET 6 sign says what this level needs. Three speech bubbles lie on the ground, and a brick wall with a lock stands past them. Walk through it and the lock takes your three. This time no tray lies behind it, and the NO TRAY. THEY ARE GONE sign says so.

Further on, the exit lock is a second brick wall away. Walk into it with an empty count and it stays shut. Three more speech bubbles sit along a ledge you reach by the ladder. Take them, come back down, and the exit lock opens. You walk on into the ending.

There are seven coins along the ground, worth ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Leave the tray out. This level uses the same lock block as level 1, and a lock only takes. Nothing in the map adds to the counter after it, so what the lock took stays taken.
  • Six words. The map holds three words before the first lock and three more on the ledge, and two locks take three each. A map with only five would leave the exit lock shut for good, and the Level check's Counters that run out would say so.
  • The lock is the door. Open words.gam in the game editor. The level's only link starts on the exit lock's own block. A lock is solid until it is paid, then it becomes sky, and the next step into that block is the link to the next scene.
  • A fresh count. Counters travel from level to level. Level 1 ends with the count at zero, so this level starts at zero.
  • The ledge. The extra words wait up a ladder, in plain sight from the ground.

pages.head: What Game-Maker cannot do
pages.html:
What Game-Maker cannot do

A lock and a tray are two blocks and a counter, and that is all:

  • A lock cannot keep part of a payment, and a tray cannot return part of one. A touch changes the counter by one fixed amount, or it is refused. The game's own touch rule (PLAYGAME.C, DoBlockTouchChar) refuses any touch that would leave a special counter at zero or below, and otherwise adds the amount in full.
  • A tray does not know what a lock took. It gives its own number, three, even if you paid something else. If the lock's price changes, change the tray to match.
  • A touch cannot read the counter and decide. Nothing here says give back half or give back whatever was paid.
  • The player does not see the counter. The status line shows hit points, lives and score, not a special counter. Put the price in the picture, as the lock does with its three notches.
  • A counter cannot go below zero, so a lock can never put you in debt.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

  • Change the tray's amount to 2 in the blocks editor. The second lock now cannot open, and the Level check says the counter runs out.
  • Change the tray to give 5. Level 1 now leaves you with two spare words after the second lock.
  • Take the tray out of level 1's map and put a bubble past the first lock instead.
  • Put a tray into level 2 behind the first lock. Three words are now enough for the whole level.
  • Move the tray up onto a ledge, then see that a player can walk right past it.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.tagline: A lock takes three. A tray gives them back.
box.back: A small explorer in a blue beanie finds speech bubbles lying about. Each one adds a word to a count. A lock takes three of them, and a gold tray beyond it can hand them back. In the second room there is no tray, so every word counts. Read the signs, then open the game in Game-Maker and change a price.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
A lock spends words, a tray gives them back
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: Two short levels about locks that take a count. Speech bubbles add words to a count, a lock takes three, and a tray past the lock can give them back. In the second level there is no tray, so what a lock takes is gone. Signs in the levels say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and change a price.
